key_insight: Ideal liquid crystal elastomer theory links molecular anisotropy to reversible actuation and soft deformation through a continuous family of stress-free states.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports constitutive modeling of LCE actuators and compliant structures whose mechanical response depends on mesogen orientation and domain rearrangement.
method: Connect anisotropic Gaussian-chain statistics to neo-classical continuum elasticity.
Explain spontaneous deformation and stripe-domain formation through non-quasi-convex free energy.
Use quasi-convex relaxation to classify polydomain responses into three stretch-dependent phases.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a theoretical review and phase classification, but reports no experimental datasets or quantitative validation.
watch_item: Ideal softness assumes no memory of the crosslinking state; practical simulations may require nonideality, director-gradient elasticity, and temperature- or rate-dependent effects.
paper_title: Elastic theory of ideal liquid crystal elastomers
